sentences.zh: 列傳第六 ○歡都子 謀演 冶訶子 阿魯補 骨赧 訛古乃 蒲查

translations.literal: Biographies 6 ○ Huandu and son Mouyan, Yehe and son Alubu, Gu Nan, E Gunai, Pu Cha
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 6: Huandu and his son Mouyan; Yehe and his son Alubu; Gu Nan; E Gunai; Pu Cha

sentences.zh: 歡都，完顏部人。

translations.literal: Huandu was a man of the Wanyan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu was of the Wanyan tribe.

sentences.zh: 祖石魯，與昭祖同時同部同名，交相得，誓曰：「生則同川居，死則同穀葬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shilu lived in the same age, the same tribe, and bore the same name as Zhaozu; they took a liking to each other and swore: "While we live we shall dwell on the same river; when we die we shall be buried in the same valley."
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shilu was Zhaozu's contemporary, clansman, and namesake; the two became fast friends and swore an oath: "In life we shall share one river's bank; in death one valley's grave."

sentences.zh: 」土人呼昭祖為勇石魯，呼石魯為賢石魯。

translations.literal: " The people called Zhaozu "Brave Shilu" and called Shilu "Virtuous Shilu."
translations.idiomatic: " The people called Zhaozu "Brave Shilu" and Shilu "Virtuous Shilu."

sentences.zh: 初，烏薩紮部有美女名罷敵悔，青嶺東混同江蜀束水人掠而去，生二女，長曰達回，幼曰滓賽。

translations.literal: In the beginning the Usazha tribe had a beautiful woman named Badihui; men of the Shushui east of Qingling on the Hun Tong River carried her off, and she bore two daughters, the elder named Dahui and the younger Zisai.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the Usazha clan had a renowned beauty named Badihui, whom raiders from the Shushui east of Qingling on the Hun Tong carried away. She bore two daughters, the elder Dahui and the younger Zisai.

sentences.zh: 昭祖與石魯謀取之，遂偕至嶺右，炷火於箭端而射。

translations.literal: Zhaozu and Shilu plotted to take them, went together to the right of the ridge, lit fire on the arrowheads, and shot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu and Shilu plotted to recover them, went together beyond the ridge, and shot arrows tipped with burning tinder.

sentences.zh: 蜀束水人怪之，皆走險阻，久之，無所複見，卻還所居。

translations.literal: The Shushui people found it strange; all fled to difficult terrain; after a long while nothing more was seen, and they returned to where they lived.
translations.idiomatic: The Shushui people took this for an evil omen and all fled into rough country. After a long interval with no further sign of them, Zhaozu and Shilu withdrew to their own settlements.

sentences.zh: 昭祖及石魯以眾至，攻取其貲產，虜二女子以歸。

translations.literal: Zhaozu and Shilu came with their forces, seized their goods, and carried off the two women.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu and Shilu then marched in force, seized their goods, and carried off the two women.

sentences.zh: 昭祖納其一，賢石魯納其一，皆以為妾。

translations.literal: Zhaozu took one and Virtuous Shilu the other, each as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozu took one for himself and Virtuous Shilu the other; each made his a concubine.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸部不肯用條教，昭祖耀武於青嶺、白山，入于蘇濱、耶懶之地，賢石魯佐之也。

translations.literal: At that time the tribes would not accept regulations; Zhaozu displayed martial prowess at Qingling and White Mountain and entered the lands of Subin and Yelan, and Virtuous Shilu assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes still refused law and custom. Zhaozu showed his strength at Qingling and White Mountain and pressed into Subin and Yelan, with Virtuous Shilu at his side throughout.

sentences.zh: 其後別去。

translations.literal: Later they parted ways.
translations.idiomatic: Later the two men went their separate ways.

sentences.zh: 至景祖時，石魯之子劾孫舉部來歸，居於安出虎水源胡凱山南。

translations.literal: In the time of Jingzu, Shilu's son He Sun brought his whole tribe to submit and dwelt south of Hukai Mountain on the Anchu River.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzu's day Shilu's son He Sun brought his tribe in submission and settled south of Hukai Mountain on the headwaters of the Anchu River.

sentences.zh: 胡凱山者，所謂和陵之地是也。

translations.literal: Hukai Mountain is what is called the land of Heling.
translations.idiomatic: Hukai Mountain is the country known as Heling.

sentences.zh: 歡都，劾孫子。

translations.literal: Huandu was He Sun's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu was He Sun's grandson.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，襲節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign he inherited the office of military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu first came to power, Huandu inherited the post of military governor.

sentences.zh: 而跋黑以屬尊，蓄異謀，不可制。

translations.literal: But Bahei, by reason of senior kinship, harbored other designs and could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Bahei, however, stood high in the lineage and nursed designs of his own; he could not be brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 諸部不肯受約束，相繼為變。

translations.literal: The tribes would not accept restraint and rose in rebellion one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Tribe after tribe refused obedience and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 歡都入與謀議，出臨戰陣，未嘗去左右。

translations.literal: Huandu went in to counsel on plans and went out to face the battle lines, never leaving Shizu's side.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu came in to counsel and went out to command on the field; he never left Shizu's side.

sentences.zh: 斡勒部人杯乃，自景祖時與其兄弟俱居安出虎水之北，及烏春作難，杯乃將與烏春合，間誘斡魯紺出水居人與之相結，欲先除去歡都。

translations.literal: Beinai of the Wole tribe, since Jingzu's time he and his brothers had all dwelt north of the Anchu River; when Wuchun made trouble, Beinai was about to join Wuchun and between whiles enticed the water-dwellers of Woluguan to link with him, wishing first to remove Huandu.
translations.idiomatic: Beinai of the Wole clan had lived with his brothers north of the Anchu River since Jingzu's day. When Wuchun rebelled, Beinai was ready to join him and secretly won over the Woluguan water-folk, intending to destroy Huandu first.

sentences.zh: 會其家被火，陰約隸人不歌束，詭稱放火乃歡都、胡土二人，使注都來謂世祖曰：「不歌束來告曰'前日之火，歡都等縱之'。

translations.literal: When his house caught fire, he secretly arranged with the bondservant Bugesou, falsely claiming the arsonists were Huandu and Hugu, and sent Zhudu to tell Shizu: "Bugesou comes to report that the fire of the other day was set by Huandu and the rest."
translations.idiomatic: When his house burned, he secretly suborned the bondservant Bugesou to claim that Huandu and Hugu had set the blaze, and sent Zhudu to Shizu with the message: "Bugesou reports that the fire the other day was the work of Huandu and his party."

sentences.zh: 若不棄舊好，其執縱火之人以來。

translations.literal: If you do not abandon the old friendship, seize those who set the fire and bring them.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not break the old bond of friendship, seize the arsonists and deliver them."

sentences.zh: 」世祖疑之。

translations.literal: " Shizu was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizu was doubtful.

sentences.zh: 石盧斡勒勃堇曰：「杯乃兄弟也，豈以一二人之故，而與兄弟構怨乎。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Shilu Wole said: "Beinai is your brother—would you for one or two men bear enmity against a brother?
translations.idiomatic: The Wole tribal chief Shilu Wole said: "Beinai is your brother. Would you for the sake of one or two men make an enemy of your own kin?

sentences.zh: 彼自取之，又將尤誰，不如與之便。

translations.literal: He brought it on himself—against whom will he complain? Better to yield to him.
translations.idiomatic: He brought this on himself. Whom else can he blame? Better to give way to him."

sentences.zh: 」歡都被甲執戟而起曰：「彼為亂之人也，若取太師兄弟，則亦與之乎。

translations.literal: " Huandu donned armor, took up his halberd, and rose, saying: "He is a man of disorder. If they take the Grand Preceptor's brothers, will you hand them over too?
translations.idiomatic: " Huandu buckled on armor, seized his halberd, and rose. "He is a rebel. If they demand the Grand Preceptor's brothers, will you surrender them as well?

sentences.zh: 今取我輩，我輩決不可往，若必用戰，當盡力致死。

translations.literal: If they take us now, we absolutely will not go. If battle is necessary, we shall fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: If they demand us, we will never go. If it must come to war, we shall fight to the last man."

sentences.zh: 」穆宗曰：「壯哉歡都，以我所見，正如此爾。

translations.literal: " Muzong said: "How stalwart is Huandu! From what I see, it is exactly so.
translations.idiomatic: " Muzong said: "How bold Huandu is! In my judgment he is entirely right.

sentences.zh: 」贈歡都以馬，曰：「戰則乘此。

translations.literal: " He gifted Huandu a horse, saying: "In battle ride this.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave Huandu a horse and said: "When you fight, ride this one.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆稱善。

translations.literal: " All praised the decision.
translations.idiomatic: " All approved.

sentences.zh: 世祖乃往見杯乃，隔鱉刺水而與之言曰：「不歌束既告縱火由歡都等，謹當如約。

translations.literal: Shizu then went to see Beinai, and across the Biecih River spoke to him: "Since Bugesou has reported that the arson was by Huandu and the others, I shall strictly keep the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu then went to Beinai and, standing across the Biecih River, said: "Bugesou has named Huandu and the rest as the arsonists. I shall keep our agreement to the letter.

sentences.zh: 當先遣不歌束來。

translations.literal: Bugesou must be sent first.
translations.idiomatic: Send Bugesou to me first."

sentences.zh: 」不歌束至，世祖于馬前殺之，使杯乃見之。

translations.literal: " When Bugesou arrived, Shizu killed him before his horse and had Beinai see it.
translations.idiomatic: " When Bugesou came, Shizu struck him down before his horse and made Beinai witness it.

sentences.zh: 既而聞之，放火者杯乃家人阿出胡山也，杯乃欲開此釁，故以誣歡都雲。

translations.literal: Later it was learned that the one who set the fire was Beinai's household servant Achuhusan; Beinai wished to open this quarrel and therefore falsely accused Huandu.
translations.idiomatic: It later came out that the fire had been set by Beinai's servant Achuhusan. Beinai had sought a pretext for strife and had framed Huandu.

sentences.zh: 臘醅、麻產與世祖遇于野鵲水。

translations.literal: Lapei and Machan encountered Shizu at the Wild Magpie River.
translations.idiomatic: Lapei and Machan met Shizu at the Wild Magpie River.

sentences.zh: 日已曛，惟從五六十騎，歡都入敵陣鏖擊之，左右出入者數四，世祖中創乃止。

translations.literal: The sun had set; Shizu had only fifty or sixty horsemen with him; Huandu charged into the enemy ranks and fought fiercely, going in and out several times; Shizu was wounded and only then did they stop.
translations.idiomatic: Dusk had fallen and Shizu had barely fifty or sixty riders. Huandu plunged into the enemy line and fought back and forth four times over before Shizu, wounded, called a halt.

sentences.zh: 烏春、窩謀罕據活刺渾水，世祖既許之降，遂還軍。

translations.literal: Wuchun and Womouhan held the Huocihun River; Shizu had already promised them submission and therefore withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun and Womouhan held the Huocihun River. Shizu had already accepted their surrender and marched his army home.

sentences.zh: 於是騷臘勃堇、富者撻懶歡勝負不助軍，而騷臘、撻懶先曾與臘醅、麻產合，世祖欲因軍還而遂滅之，馳馬前進。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribal chiefs Saolai and the wealthy Tadalian rejoiced in the outcome and did not aid the army; yet Saolai and Tadalian had earlier joined with Lapei and Machan; Shizu wished to destroy them on the army's return and spurred his horse forward.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs Saolai and the wealthy Tadalian had stood aside from the fight, though both had once sided with Lapei and Machan. Shizu meant to destroy them on the march home and spurred his horse forward.

sentences.zh: 撻懶者，貞惠皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Tadalian was the younger brother of Empress Zhenhui.
translations.idiomatic: Tadalian was Empress Zhenhui's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 歡都下馬執轡而諫曰：「獨不念愛弟蒲陽溫與弟婦乎。

translations.literal: Huandu dismounted, took the reins, and remonstrated: "Will you not think of your beloved younger brother Puyangwen and his wife?
translations.idiomatic: Huandu dismounted, seized the bridle, and pleaded: "Have you no thought for your dear young brother Puyangwen and his wife?

sentences.zh: 」世祖感其言，遂止。

translations.literal: " Shizu was moved by his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizu was moved and drew rein.

sentences.zh: 蒲陽溫者，漢語雲幼弟也。

translations.literal: Puyangwen, in Chinese, means "younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: Puyangwen is the Jurchen name for "younger brother" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 世祖母弟中穆宗最少，故雲然。

translations.literal: Among Shizu's maternal younger brothers Muzong was the youngest, and therefore he was so called.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shizu's maternal brothers Muzong was the youngest, and so earned that name.

sentences.zh: 穆宗德歡都言，後以撻懶女曷羅哂妻其子谷神。

translations.literal: Muzong was grateful for Huandu's words; later he gave Tadalian's daughter Yiluoxiang in marriage to his son Gushen.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong held Huandu's counsel in honor and later gave Tadalian's daughter Yiluoxiang to his son Gushen in marriage.

sentences.zh: 太祖追麻產，歡都射中其首，遂獲之。

translations.literal: Taizu pursued Machan; Huandu shot him in the head and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pursued Machan, Huandu struck him in the head with an arrow and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 遼人命穆宗、太祖、辭不失、歡都俱為詳穩。

translations.literal: The Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu all as xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Liao appointed Muzong, Taizu, Cibushi, and Huandu each to the office of xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 斡善、斡脫以姑裏甸兵來歸，使斜缽勃堇撫定之。

translations.literal: Woshan and Wotuo brought the Guli troops to submit; Shizu sent the tribal chief Xiebo to pacify and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Woshan and Wotuo brought the Guli contingent in submission, and Shizu sent the tribal chief Xiebo to settle them.

sentences.zh: 蒲察部故石、拔石等，誘其眾入城，陷三百餘人。

translations.literal: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe enticed their forces into the city and trapped more than three hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Gushi, Bashi, and others of the Pucha tribe lured the troops into a city and trapped more than three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 歡都為都統，往治斜缽失軍之狀，盡解斜缽所將軍、大破烏春、窩謀罕於斜堆，擒故石、拔石。

translations.literal: Huandu served as commander-in-chief, went to deal with the circumstances of Xiebo's defeated army, fully released the troops Xiebo had led, routed Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and captured Gushi and Bashi.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu was made commander-in-chief. He went to answer for Xiebo's defeat, released all the men under Xiebo's command, broke Wuchun and Womouhan at Xiedui, and took Gushi and Bashi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 初，耶悔水納喝部撒八之弟曰阿注阿，與人爭部族官，不得直，來歸穆宗。

translations.literal: In the beginning Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Yehui Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, disputed a tribal office with another and did not obtain justice; he came to submit to Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Azu'a, younger brother of Saba of the Nahana tribe on the Yehui River, had quarreled over a tribal post and failed to obtain justice. He came in submission to Muzong.

sentences.zh: 阿注阿之甥曰三濱、曰撒達。

translations.literal: Azu'a's nephews were named Sanbin and Sada.
translations.idiomatic: Azu'a's nephews were Sanbin and Sada.

sentences.zh: 辭不失破烏春窩謀罕城，獲三濱、撒達，並獲其母，以為次室，撫其二子。

translations.literal: Cibushi captured the city of Wuchun and Womouhan, took Sanbin and Sada, and also took their mother, making her a secondary wife and nurturing the two sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Cibushi stormed the stronghold of Wuchun and Womouhan he took Sanbin and Sada and their mother as well. He made her a secondary consort and raised the two boys.

sentences.zh: 撒達告阿注阿必為變，不信而殺之。

translations.literal: Sada warned that Azu'a would surely rebel; Cibushi did not believe it and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sada warned that Azu'a would rebel. Cibushi disbelieved him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 撒達臨刑歎曰：「後必知之。

translations.literal: At execution Sada sighed: "Later they will know.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death Sada sighed: "You will know soon enough.

sentences.zh: 」至是，阿注阿果為變。

translations.literal: " By this time Azu'a did indeed rebel.
translations.idiomatic: " By then Azu'a had indeed risen in revolt.

sentences.zh: 因穆宗晨出獵，糾率七八人操兵入宅，奪據寢門，劫貞惠皇后及家人等。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of Muzong's morning hunt, he gathered seven or eight men with weapons, entered the residence, seized the sleeping quarters' gate, and held Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.
translations.idiomatic: While Muzong was out hunting at dawn, he rallied seven or eight armed men, forced their way into the palace, seized the inner gate, and took Empress Zhenhui and the household hostage.

sentences.zh: 歡都入見阿注阿曰：「汝輩所謀之事奈何。

translations.literal: Huandu went in to see Azu'a and said: "What is to become of the affair you are plotting?
translations.idiomatic: Huandu went in to Azu'a and said: "What end do you intend for this plot of yours?

sentences.zh: 閨門眷屬豈足劫質，徒使之驚恐耳。

translations.literal: Women and kin of the inner quarters are hardly fit hostages—they only frighten them for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The women of the inner quarters are poor hostages; you only terrify them to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 汝固識我，盍以我為質也。

translations.literal: You know me well—why not take me as hostage instead?
translations.idiomatic: You know me well. Take me instead."

sentences.zh: 」再三言之，阿注阿從之，貞惠皇后乃得解，而質歡都。

translations.literal: " He spoke thus again and again; Azu'a consented; Empress Zhenhui was released, and Huandu was held hostage.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed the point again and again until Azu'a agreed. The empress was freed and Huandu held in her place.

sentences.zh: 而撒改、辭不失使人告急於獵所。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Sagai and Cibushi sent men to report the emergency at the hunting grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai and Cibushi meanwhile sent word in haste to the hunt.

sentences.zh: 穆宗亦心動，罷獵。

translations.literal: Muzong's heart was also stirred, and he ended the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong's heart misgave him and he broke off the hunt.

sentences.zh: 中途逢告者，日午至，阿注阿謂穆宗曰：「可使系案女直知名官僚相結，送我兄弟親屬由咸州路入遼國，庫金廄馬與我勿惜，歡都亦當送我至遼境，然後還。

translations.literal: Midway he met the messenger; by noon he arrived. Azu'a said to Muzong: "You may have the well-known bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen join together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou route into Liao territory, give me storehouses of gold and stables of horses without stint, and Huandu must also escort me to the Liao border and then return.
translations.idiomatic: He met the messenger on the road and reached home at noon. Azu'a told Muzong: "Let the noted bureaucrats of the registered Jurchen band together, send my brothers and kin by the Xianzhou road into Liao, give me gold from the treasury and horses from the stables without stint, and let Huandu escort me to the Liao frontier before he returns.

sentences.zh: 」而耍穆宗盟，穆宗皆從之。

translations.literal: " He also forced Muzong to swear an oath, and Muzong agreed to everything.
translations.idiomatic: " He also extorted an oath from Muzong, who yielded to every demand.

sentences.zh: 遂執歡都及阿魯太彎、阿魯不太彎等七人，以衣裾相結，與阿注阿俱行，至遼境，乃釋歡都。

translations.literal: They then seized Huandu and Alutaiwan, Alutaibuwan, and six others, tied their garment skirts together, and marched with Azu'a; when they reached Liao territory they released Huandu.
translations.idiomatic: They bound Huandu together with Alutaiwan, Alutaibuwan, and five others, linking their robe-hems, and marched with Azu'a. At the Liao border they set Huandu free.

sentences.zh: 歡都至濟州，實黃龍府，使人馳驛要遮阿注阿黨屬，惟縱其親人使去。

translations.literal: Huandu reached Jizhou—in fact Huanglong Prefecture—and sent men by relay post to intercept Azu'a's followers, releasing only his kin to go.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu reached Jizhou, which was in fact Huanglong Prefecture, and sent riders by relay to cut off Azu'a's party, sparing only his kin.

sentences.zh: 遂殺三濱並其母，具報於遼，乞還阿注阿，遼人流之曷堇城。

translations.literal: He then killed Sanbin and his mother, reported fully to Liao, and begged the return of Azu'a; Liao exiled him to Yijin city.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed Sanbin and his mother, reported the whole affair to Liao, and asked that Azu'a be returned. Liao banished him to Yijin.

sentences.zh: 其後，阿注阿懷思鄉土，亡歸，附於系案女直，因亂其官僚之室，捕之，不伏，乃見殺。

translations.literal: Later Azu'a longed for his native land, fled back, attached himself to the registered Jurchen, and by disturbing the chambers of their bureaucrats was captured; he would not submit and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later, homesick for his own country, Azu'a fled back and joined the registered Jurchen. He raided the dwellings of their officials, was seized, refused to yield, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 穆宗襲位之初，諸父之子習烈、斜缽及諸兄有異言，曰：「君相之位，皆渠輩為之，奈何？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Muzong's succession, the sons of his father's brothers Xilie and Xiebo and his elder brothers had dissenting words, saying: "The positions of lord and minister were all made by them—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Early in Muzong's reign the sons of his uncles Xilie and Xiebo and his elder brothers murmured dissent: "Those men made themselves lord and minister—what of us?

sentences.zh: 」歡都曰：「汝輩若紛爭，則吾必不默默但已。

translations.literal: " Huandu said: "If you contend among yourselves, I shall certainly not remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Huandu said: "If you quarrel among yourselves, I shall not stand idly by.

sentences.zh: 」眾聞之遂帖然，自是不復有異言者。

translations.literal: " When the multitude heard this they became submissive, and from then on there were no more dissenting words.
translations.idiomatic: " At his words the company fell quiet, and from that day no one spoke out again.

sentences.zh: 歡都事四君，出入四十年，征伐之際遇敵則先戰，廣廷大議多用其謀。

translations.literal: Huandu served four rulers, coming and going for forty years; on campaigns when he met the enemy he fought first; in broad court deliberations his counsel was often used.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu served four sovereigns across forty years. In battle he always met the enemy first; in great council his counsel was often followed.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗曰：「吾有歡都，則何事不成。

translations.literal: Shizu once said: "With Huandu at my side, what affair could fail?
translations.idiomatic: Shizu once said: "With Huandu at my side, what could I not accomplish?

sentences.zh: 」肅宗時，委任冠於近僚。

translations.literal: " Under Suzong his commission ranked above the close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Suzong his trust outranked every courtier near the throne.

sentences.zh: 穆宗嗣位，凡圖遼事皆專委之。

translations.literal: When Muzong succeeded, all affairs concerning Liao were entrusted to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong came to the throne, every matter touching Liao was placed solely in his hands.

sentences.zh: 康宗以為父叔舊人，尤加敬禮，多所補益。

translations.literal: Kangzong regarded him as an old companion of his father and uncles and showed him especial respect and courtesy, benefiting greatly from him.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong treated him as a veteran of his father and uncles' generation, honored him the more, and drew great profit from his service.

sentences.zh: 康宗十一年癸巳二月，得疾，避疾于米里每水，薨，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the second month of Kangzong year 11, guisi, he fell ill, withdrew to the Milimei River to avoid illness, and died at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangzong 11 (guisi) he fell ill, withdrew to the Milimei River to convalesce, and died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，康宗親迓于路，送至其家，親視葬事。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession returned, Kangzong personally met it on the road, escorted it to his home, and personally oversaw the burial.
translations.idiomatic: When the bier came home Kangzong met it on the road, escorted it to Huandu's house, and oversaw the burial himself.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，追贈儀同三司、代國公。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year 15 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol and Duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 15 he was posthumously made Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol and Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠敏。

translations.literal: In Mingchang year 5 he was further enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol and given the posthumous title Zhongmin, "Loyal and Keen."
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol and given the posthumous name Zhongmin, Loyal and Keen.

sentences.zh: 子穀神、謀演。

translations.literal: His sons were Gushen and Mouyan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Gushen and Mouyan.

sentences.zh: 穀神別有傳。

translations.literal: Gushen has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Gushen has his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 子 謀演

translations.literal: Son: Mouyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Mouyan

sentences.zh: 謀演，當阿注阿之難，從歡都代為質。

translations.literal: Mouyan, during Azu'a's crisis, followed Huandu and served as hostage in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: During Azu'a's revolt Mouyan went with Huandu and stood hostage in his place.

sentences.zh: 後與宗峻俱侍太祖，宗峻坐謀演上，上怒，命坐其下。

translations.literal: Later he and Zongjun both attended Taizu; Zongjun sat above Mouyan; the emperor was angry and ordered him to sit below.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Zongjun both attended Taizu. Zongjun took the seat above Mouyan; the emperor was angered and ordered Mouyan seated below.

sentences.zh: 孛堇老孛論、拔合汝、轄拔速三人爭千戶，上曰：「汝輩能如歡都父子有勞于國者乎。

translations.literal: The tribal chiefs Laoluelun, Bahenu, and Xiabasu disputed over command of a thousand households; the emperor said: "Can you be like Huandu and his son, who have labored for the state?
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs Laoluelun, Bahenu, and Xiabasu quarreled over a thousand-household command. The emperor said: "Have any of you served the state as Huandu and his son have?

sentences.zh: 」乃命謀演為千戶，三人者皆隸焉，其眷顧如此。

translations.literal: " He then appointed Mouyan commander of a thousand households, and all three were placed under him—such was his favor.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Mouyan commander of a thousand households and placed all three under him—such was the regard in which the house was held.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年十二月卒，天會十五年贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth month of Tianfu year 5; in Tianhui year 15 he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of Tianfu 5 and in Tianhui 15 was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 冶訶系出景祖，居神隱水完顏部，為其部勃堇。

translations.literal: Yehe was descended from Jingzu, dwelt with the Wanyan tribe on the Shenyin River, and was tribal chief of his division.
translations.idiomatic: Yehe traced his line to Jingzu, lived with the Wanyan on the Shenyin River, and was chief of his division.

sentences.zh: 與同部人把裏勃堇，斡泯水蒲察部胡都化勃堇、廝都勃堇，泰神忒保水完顏部安團勃堇，統門水溫蒂痕部活裏蓋勃堇，俱來歸，金之為國，自此益大。

translations.literal: Together with Balai, tribal chief of the same division, Huduhua and Sidu, tribal chiefs of the Pucha tribe on the Womin River, Antuan, tribal chief of the Wanyan tribe on the Taishentebai River, and Huoligai, tribal chief of the Wendihen tribe on the Tongmen River, they all came to submit; from this the Jin state grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: With Balai of his own division, Huduhua and Sidu of the Pucha on the Womin River, Antuan of the Wanyan on the Taishentebai River, and Huoligai of the Wendihen on the Tongmen River, he all came in submission—and from that hour the Jin state grew greater still.

sentences.zh: 肅宗拒桓赧已再失利，世祖命歡都、冶訶，以本部謀克之兵助之。

translations.literal: Suzong in resisting Huanhan had already suffered defeat twice; Shizu ordered Huandu and Yehe to assist him with the commandery troops of their own tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong had twice been beaten by Huanhan. Shizu sent Huandu and Yehe with the commandery levies of their tribes to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 冶訶與歡都常在世祖左右，居則與謀議，出則泣行陣，未嘗不在其間。

translations.literal: Yehe and Huandu were constantly at Shizu's side; at rest they counseled together, in the field they wept through the ranks—never absent from his affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yehe and Huandu were ever at Shizu's side—in council by day, in the battle line by night, never far from his affairs.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year 15 he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 15 he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver-Green Tally.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，贈特進，諡忠濟，與代國公歡都、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，俱配享世祖廟廷。

translations.literal: In Mingchang year 5 he was further enfeoffed as Special Advancement with the posthumous title Zhongji, "Loyal and Succoring," and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol Bada, all received collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 5 he was raised to Special Advancement with the posthumous name Zhongji, Loyal and Succoring, and together with Duke of Dai Huandu, Special Advancement Hezhe, Grand Master of the Palace Penna, and Bearer of the Triple Staff Bada was granted collateral sacrifice in Shizu's temple.

sentences.zh: 冶訶子阿魯補、骨赧、訛古乃、散荅。

translations.literal: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gu Nan, E Gunai, and Sanda.
translations.idiomatic: Yehe's sons were Alubu, Gu Nan, E Gunai, and Sanda.

sentences.zh: 散荅子蒲查。

translations.literal: Sanda's son was Pu Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Sanda's son was Pu Cha.

sentences.zh: 子 阿魯補

translations.literal: Son: Alubu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Alubu

sentences.zh: 阿魯補，冶訶之子。

translations.literal: Alubu was Yehe's son.
translations.idiomatic: Alubu was Yehe's son.

sentences.zh: 為人魁偉多智略，勇於戰。

translations.literal: As a man he was tall and imposing, full of stratagems, and bold in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of imposing stature and keen stratagem, fearless in battle.

sentences.zh: 未冠從軍，下咸州、東京。

translations.literal: Before coming of age he followed the army and captured Xianzhou and Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age he took the field and helped reduce Xianzhou and Dongjing.

sentences.zh: 遼人來取海州，從勃堇麻吉往援，道遇重敵，力戰，斬首千級。

translations.literal: When the Liao came to retake Haizhou, he followed the tribal chief Maji to relieve it; on the road they met a strong enemy and fought fiercely, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao marched to recover Haizhou he went with the tribal chief Maji to its relief, met a heavy enemy force on the road, fought hard, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 從斡魯古攻豪、懿州，以十餘騎破敵七百，進襲遼主。

translations.literal: He followed Wolugu in attacking Hao and Yizhou, with a dozen horsemen broke seven hundred of the enemy, and pressed on to strike the Liao emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wolugu against Hao and Yizhou, routed seven hundred men with barely a dozen riders, and pressed the attack on the Liao emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 阿魯補徇北地，招降營帳二十四，民戶數千。

translations.literal: Alubu swept the northern country, receiving the submission of twenty-four encampments and several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Alubu ranged the northern lands and won over twenty-four encampments and several thousand households.

sentences.zh: 時已下西京，闍母攻應州未下，退營於州北十餘裏，夜遣阿魯補率兵四百伺敵，城中果出兵三千平襲，阿魯補道與之遇，斬首百余，獲馬六十。

translations.literal: The Western Capital had already been taken; Zhamu attacked Yingzhou without success, withdrew and encamped more than ten li north of the city, and by night sent Alubu with four hundred men to watch the enemy; the city indeed sent out three thousand in a surprise attack; Alubu met them on the road, beheaded more than a hundred, and seized sixty horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Capital had fallen. Zhamu failed to take Yingzhou and withdrew to camp north of the city. That night he sent Alubu with four hundred men to scout. The garrison sallied with three thousand in a surprise attack; Alubu met them on the road, took more than a hundred heads, and captured sixty horses.

sentences.zh: 後遼兵三萬出馬邑之境，以千兵擊之，斬其將於陣。

translations.literal: Later thirty thousand Liao troops came out from the borders of Mayi; with a thousand men he attacked them and beheaded their general in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand Liao troops marched from Mayi, he met them with a thousand men, broke their line, and killed their general on the field.

sentences.zh: 天會初，宋王宗望討張覺于平州，聞應州有兵萬餘來援，遣阿魯補與阿裏帶迎擊之，斬馘數千而還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhui, Prince of Song Zongwang campaigned against Zhang Jue at Pingzhou; hearing that more than ten thousand troops from Yingzhou were coming to relieve him, he sent Alubu and Alidai to meet and attack them, beheading several thousand before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianhui, Zongwang, Prince of Song, marched against Zhang Jue at Pingzhou. Learning that more than ten thousand men from Yingzhou were marching to his aid, he sent Alubu and Alidai to intercept them; they took several thousand heads and returned.

sentences.zh: 複從其兄虞劃，率兵三千攻乾州，虞劃道病卒，代領其眾，至乾州，降其軍及營帳三十，獲印四十，與僕虺攻下義州。

translations.literal: He again followed his elder brother Yu Hua, leading three thousand men to attack Qianzhou; Yu Hua died of illness on the road; Alubu took command of his force; reaching Qianzhou he received the surrender of their army and thirty encampments, seized forty seals, and with Puhui captured Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed his elder brother Yu Hua with three thousand men against Qianzhou. Yu Hua died on the march and Alubu took over his command. At Qianzhou he received the surrender of the garrison and thirty encampments, seized forty seals, and with Puhui reduced Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 宗望伐宋，與郭藥師戰于白河。

translations.literal: Zongwang campaigned against Song and fought Guo Yaoshi at the White River.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang marched on Song he fought Guo Yaoshi at the White River.

sentences.zh: 宗望命阿魯補以二謀克先登，奮戰，賞賚特異。

translations.literal: Zongwang ordered Alubu to lead two commanderies in the first assault; he fought fiercely and received exceptional rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang ordered Alubu to lead two commanderies in the first assault. He fought with exceptional valor and was rewarded beyond the common measure.

sentences.zh: 至汴，破淮南援兵，斬其二將。

translations.literal: Reaching Bian, he defeated the Huainan relief troops and beheaded two of their generals.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian he routed the Huainan relief force and killed two of its generals.

sentences.zh: 大軍退次孟陽。

translations.literal: The great army withdrew and encamped at Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The main army withdrew to Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 姚平仲夜以重兵來襲，阿魯補適當其中，力戰敗之。

translations.literal: Yao Pingzhong came by night with a heavy force to attack; Alubu happened to be in their path and fought fiercely to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Pingzhong struck by night with a heavy force. Alubu stood directly in their path, fought hard, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 既還，聞大名、開德合兵十余萬來爭河。

translations.literal: After returning, he heard that Daming and Kaide had combined more than a hundred thousand troops to contest the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he learned that Daming and Kaide had united more than a hundred thousand men to contest the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 至河上，知去敵尚遠，乃以輕兵夜發，詰旦至衛縣，遇敵，斬首數千級，餘皆潰去。

translations.literal: Reaching the river and knowing the enemy was still far off, he sent light troops by night; at dawn he reached Weixian, met the enemy, beheaded several thousand, and the rest all fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the river he saw the enemy was still distant and sent light troops by night. By dawn he reached Weixian, met the foe, took several thousand heads, and put the rest to flight.

sentences.zh: 師次邢州，滹沱橋已焚，阿魯補先以偏師營于水上，比軍至而橋成。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xingzhou; the Hutuo bridge had been burned; Alubu first camped a detached force on the water, and by the time the army arrived the bridge was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Xingzhou, where the Hutuo bridge had been burned. Alubu threw a detachment across the water first; by the time the main body arrived the bridge was finished.

sentences.zh: 宗望嘉其功，出真定庫物賞之，為長勝軍千戶。

translations.literal: Zongwang praised his merit, drew goods from the Zhending treasury to reward him, and made him commander of a thousand households in the Ever-Victorious Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang praised his service, rewarded him from the Zhending treasury, and made him a thousand-household commander in the Ever-Victorious Army.

sentences.zh: 及再伐宋，從宗望破敵于井陘，遂下欒城。

translations.literal: When Song was attacked again, he followed Zongwang in defeating the enemy at Jingxing and then took Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the second campaign against Song he followed Zongwang, broke the enemy at Jingxing, and took Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 師自大名濟河，阿魯補屯於洺州之境。

translations.literal: The army crossed the river from Daming; Alubu encamped in the territory of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed from Daming; Alubu held the approaches to Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時康王留相州，大名府以兵來攻我營，阿魯補乘夜以騎二百潛出其後，反擊敗之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Kang remained at Xiangzhou; troops from Daming Prefecture came to attack our camp; Alubu by night with two hundred horsemen stole out behind them and counterattacked to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang was then at Xiangzhou. Daming sent troops against the Jin camp; Alubu took two hundred horsemen by night, slipped behind them, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 居數日，敵複來，蘇統制以兵二萬先至，阿魯補乘其未集，以三百騎出戰，大敗其眾，生擒蘇統制，殺之。

translations.literal: After several days the enemy came again; Commander Su with twenty thousand men arrived first; Alubu, seizing them before they had fully gathered, went out with three hundred horsemen, routed their force, captured Commander Su alive, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the enemy returned. Commander Su arrived first with twenty thousand men. Alubu struck before they could mass, rode out with three hundred horsemen, shattered their force, took Su alive, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 大軍既克汴京，攻洺州，敗大名救兵，遂下洺州。

translations.literal: After the great army had taken Bianjing, they attacked Mingzhou, defeated Daming's relief troops, and then took Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Bianjing fell the army attacked Mingzhou, routed Daming's relief force, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 從撻懶文攻恩州還，洺人複叛，阿魯補先至城下，城中出兵來戰，敗之，執其守佐，，遂與蒲魯懽取信德軍。

translations.literal: Returning from following Tadawen's attack on Enzhou, the people of Mingzhou rebelled again; Alubu reached the city first; the city sent troops out to fight and he defeated them, seized their defending officials, and then with Puluhuan took Xinde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Tadawen's campaign against Enzhou, Mingzhou rose again. Alubu reached the walls first, defeated a sally, seized the defending officials, and with Puluhuan took Xinde.

sentences.zh: 梁王宗弼取開德，阿魯補以步兵五千赴之。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Zongbi took Kaide; Alubu went to his aid with five thousand foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi, Prince of Liang, took Kaide, and Alubu marched to his support with five thousand foot.

sentences.zh: 大名境內多盜，命阿魯補留屯其地。

translations.literal: Bandits were numerous within Daming territory; he was ordered to remain and garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in Daming, and he was ordered to remain and garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 賊犯莘縣，聞阿魯補至，即潰去，追襲一晝夜，至館陶及之，皆俘以歸。

translations.literal: Bandits raided Shenxian; hearing Alubu had come they at once fled; he pursued for a day and a night, overtook them at Guantao, and took them all prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits struck Shenxian but scattered at word of Alubu's approach. He pursued a day and a night, overtook them at Guantao, and took them all prisoner.

sentences.zh: 從宗弼襲康王，即渡淮，阿魯補以兵四千留和州，總督江、淮間戍將，以討未附郡縣。

translations.literal: Following Zongbi in the pursuit of Prince Kang, they crossed the Huai at once; Alubu remained at Hezhou with four thousand men, overseeing the garrison commanders between the Yangzi and Huai to subdue counties not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zongbi in the pursuit of Prince Kang and crossed the Huai. Alubu remained at Hezhou with four thousand men, commanding the garrisons between the Yangzi and Huai to bring in counties still holding out.

sentences.zh: 遂攻下太平州，隳其城。

translations.literal: He then attacked and took Taipingzhou and demolished its walls.
translations.idiomatic: He took Taipingzhou and razed its walls.

sentences.zh: 廬州叛，以偏師討之，敗其騎六千，擒三校。

translations.literal: Luzhou rebelled; with a detached force he campaigned against it, defeated six thousand of their horsemen, and captured three commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou rebelled he led a detachment against it, routed six thousand horsemen, and took three commanders prisoner.

sentences.zh: 明日複破敵二萬於慎縣，斬首五百。

translations.literal: The next day he again defeated twenty thousand of the enemy at Shenxian and beheaded five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he broke twenty thousand of the enemy at Shenxian and took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 張永合步騎數萬來戰，阿魯補兵止二千，敵圍之，阿魯補潰圍力戰，竟敗之，追殺四十裏，獲馬三百而還。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong combined infantry and cavalry numbering tens of thousands to give battle; Alubu had only two thousand men; the enemy surrounded them; Alubu broke out of the encirclement and fought fiercely, finally defeating them, pursued and killed for forty li, seized three hundred horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong brought tens of thousands of foot and horse against him. Alubu had only two thousand and was surrounded. He burst the ring, fought through, routed the enemy, pursued forty li, and returned with three hundred captured horses.

sentences.zh: 再攻廬州，與迪古不敗敵萬眾於拓皋，至廬州，騎兵五百出戰，敗之，斬其二校。

translations.literal: Attacking Luzhou again, he and Digubu defeated ten thousand of the enemy at Tuogao; reaching Luzhou, five hundred horsemen came out to fight; he defeated them and beheaded two commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Luzhou again. With Digubu he broke ten thousand men at Tuogao. At the city walls five hundred horsemen sallied; he defeated them and killed two commanders.

sentences.zh: 師還。

translations.literal: The army returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched home.

sentences.zh: 宗弼趨陝西，道聞大名複叛，遣阿魯補經略之，獨與譯者至城下，招之，大名果降。

translations.literal: Zongbi hurried toward Shaanxi; on the road he heard Daming had rebelled again and sent Alubu to manage the matter; Alubu went alone with an interpreter to the foot of the walls and summoned them; Daming indeed submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi hurried west toward Shaanxi. On the road he learned Daming had rebelled again and sent Alubu to deal with it. Alubu went to the walls alone with an interpreter, called on the city to yield, and Daming submitted.

sentences.zh: 翌日，下令民間兵器，悉上送官，於是吏民按堵如故。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered that weapons among the people all be handed up to the authorities; officials and commoners then lived in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered all private weapons surrendered to the authorities, and officials and people alike returned to their former quiet.

sentences.zh: 為大名開德路都統。

translations.literal: He became commander-in-chief of the Daming-Kaide circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander-in-chief of the Daming-Kaide circuit.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，阿魯補屯兵於汴城外。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, Alubu garrisoned troops outside the walls of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi puppet state was set up, Alubu encamped his troops outside Bian.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年，詔廢齊國，已執劉麟，阿魯補先入汴京備變。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year 15 an edict abolished the Qi state; Liu Lin had already been seized; Alubu entered Bianjing first to guard against disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 15 an edict abolished Qi. Liu Lin was already in custody, and Alubu entered Bianjing first to guard against trouble.

sentences.zh: 明年，除歸德尹。

translations.literal: The following year he was made prefect of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed prefect of Guide.

sentences.zh: 割河南地與宋，入為燕京內省使。

translations.literal: When the lands south of the river were ceded to Song, he entered the capital as Inner Secretariat envoy of Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the lands south of the river were ceded to Song, he entered service as Inner Secretariat envoy at Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 宗弼複河南，阿魯補先濟河，撫定諸郡，再為歸德尹、河南路都統。

translations.literal: When Zongbi recovered the lands south of the river, Alubu crossed the river first, pacified and settled the prefectures, and again became prefect of Guide and commander-in-chief of the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi recovered the south, Alubu crossed the river first, pacified the prefectures, and again became prefect of Guide and commander-in-chief of Henan.

sentences.zh: 宋兵來取河南地，宗弼召阿魯補，與許州韓常、潁州大臭、陳州赤盞暉、皆會于汴，阿魯補以敵在近，獨不赴。

translations.literal: Song troops came to recover the lands south of the river; Zongbi summoned Alubu, Han Chang of Xuzhou, Dachou of Yingzhou, and Chisan Hui of Chenzhou to assemble at Bian; Alubu, because the enemy was near, alone did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Song troops came to recover the south. Zongbi summoned Alubu, Han Chang of Xuzhou, Dachou of Yingzhou, and Chisan Hui of Chenzhou to assemble at Bian. Alubu alone stayed away, for the enemy was at his gates.

sentences.zh: 而宋將岳飛、劉光世等，果乘間襲取許潁三州，旁郡皆回應。

translations.literal: Song generals Yue Fei, Liu Guangshi, and others indeed seized the opportunity to strike and take the three prefectures of Xu, Ying, and Chen; neighboring commanderies all responded in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Song generals Yue Fei, Liu Guangshi, and others did seize the moment, took Xu, Ying, and Chen, and neighboring districts rose in support.

sentences.zh: 其兵犯歸德者，阿魯補連擊敗之，複取亳、宿等州，河南平，阿魯補功最。

translations.literal: Those of their troops that invaded Guide, Alubu repeatedly defeated; he recovered Bo, Su, and other prefectures; the south was pacified, and Alubu's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: The columns that threatened Guide he beat back again and again, retook Bo, Su, and other prefectures, and pacified the south—no man's service surpassed his.

sentences.zh: 皇統五年，為行台參知政事，授世襲猛安，兼合紮謀克。

translations.literal: In Huangtong year 5 he became Associate Administrator of the Branch Secretariat, was granted a hereditary meng'an, and concurrently held a combined commandery post.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 5 he became Associate Administrator of the Branch Secretariat, received a hereditary meng'an, and held a combined commandery command.

sentences.zh: 改元帥右監軍，婆速路統軍，歸德軍節度使，累階儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Army Supervisor of the Marshal's Office, commander of the Basu circuit, military governor of Guide Army, and rose by stages to Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Army Supervisor of the Marshal's Office, commander of the Basu circuit, and military governor of Guide, rising by stages to Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol.

sentences.zh: 其在汴時，嘗取官舍材木，構私第於恩州，至是事覺，法當「議勳」「議親」。

translations.literal: While at Bian he had once taken timber from government buildings and built a private residence at Enzhou; by now the matter came to light; by law it called for deliberation on merit and on kinship.
translations.idiomatic: While at Bian he had taken timber from government buildings and built a private house at Enzhou. The affair now came to light. By law the case called for deliberation on merit and on kinship.

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗在軍中，惡阿魯補，詔曰：「若論勳勞，更有過於此者。

translations.literal: Hailing had once been in the army and disliked Alubu; an edict said: "If one considers merit and labor, there are those who have done more than this.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing, who had once served in the ranks and disliked Alubu, decreed: "Measured by merit and service, others have done more than this.

sentences.zh: 況官至一品，足以酬之。

translations.literal: Moreover his office has reached the first rank, which is sufficient recompense.
translations.idiomatic: His rank already stands at the first grade, reward enough in itself.

sentences.zh: 國家立法，貴賤一也，豈以親貴而有異也。

translations.literal: The state establishes law; noble and base are one; how could there be difference because of kinship and eminence?
translations.idiomatic: The state's law makes no distinction between high and low. Kinship and rank cannot set it aside."

sentences.zh: 」遂論死。

translations.literal: " He was therefore sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: He was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 年五十五。

translations.literal: He was fifty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 阿魯補以將家子從征伐，屢立功，曆官有惠愛，得民心。

translations.literal: Alubu, as the son of a military family, followed the campaigns and repeatedly achieved merit; in his successive offices he showed kindness and won the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Born to a warrior house, Alubu followed campaign after campaign and won repeated distinction. In every post he ruled with kindness and won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 及死，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: At his death all mourned him.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，贈儀同三司，詔以其子為右衛將軍，襲猛安及親管謀克，賜銀五百兩、重彩二十端、絹三百匹。

translations.literal: In Dading year 3 he was posthumously made Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol; an edict made his son Right Guard General, inheriting the meng'an and personally administered commandery, and granted five hundred taels of silver, twenty bolts of heavy brocade, and three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 3 he was posthumously made Bearer of the Triple Staff with Equal Protocol. His son was appointed Right Guard General, inherited the meng'an and personal commandery, and received five hundred taels of silver, twenty bolts of heavy brocade, and three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 子 骨赧

translations.literal: Son: Gu Nan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Gu Nan

sentences.zh: 骨赧，冶訶子，善騎射，有材幹。

translations.literal: Gu Nan was Yehe's son, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and possessed of ability.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Nan, Yehe's son, was skilled in horsemanship and archery and gifted with ability.

sentences.zh: 從討桓赧散達、烏春、窩謀罕、留可之叛，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in suppressing the rebellions of Huanhan, Sandá, Wuchun, Womouhan, and Liuke, and in each achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in suppressing the rebellions of Huanhan, Sandá, Wuchun, Womouhan, and Liuke and distinguished himself in each.

sentences.zh: 從太祖伐遼，骨赧從軍戰甯江州出河店，破遼主親軍，皆以力戰受賞，襲其父謀克。

translations.literal: Following Taizu in the campaign against Liao, Gu Nan followed the army in fighting at Ningjiangzhou and Chuhedian, defeated the Liao emperor's personal troops, and in each case was rewarded for fierce fighting; he inherited his father's commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned against Liao, Gu Nan fought at Ningjiangzhou and Chuhedian, broke the Liao emperor's personal guard, and was rewarded each time for valor in battle. He inherited his father's commandery.

sentences.zh: 領秦王宗翰千戶，攻下中、西兩京。

translations.literal: He led the thousand households of Prince of Qin Zonghan and captured the Central and Western capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He led a thousand households under Zonghan, Prince of Qin, and helped take the Central and Western capitals.

sentences.zh: 宗翰伐宋，圍太原未下，宗翰還西京，骨赧以右翼軍佐銀術可守太原。

translations.literal: Zonghan campaigned against Song and besieged Taiyuan without taking it; Zonghan returned to the Western Capital; Gu Nan with the right wing assisted Yinshu Ke in defending Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan marched on Song he besieged Taiyuan without success and returned to the Western Capital. Gu Nan held Taiyuan with the right wing under Yinshu Ke.

sentences.zh: 是時汾州、團柏、榆次、嵐、憲、潞皆有兵來援，骨赧凡四戰，皆破之。

translations.literal: At that time Fenzhou, Tuanbai, Yuci, Lan, Xian, and Lu all sent troops to relieve the city; Gu Nan fought four battles and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Relief columns came from Fenzhou, Tuanbai, Yuci, Lan, Xian, and Lu. Gu Nan fought four engagements and won them all.

sentences.zh: 大軍團汴，骨赧引萬戶軍，屢敗其援兵。

translations.literal: The great army besieged Bian; Gu Nan led the ten-thousand-household army and repeatedly defeated their relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army besieged Bian, Gu Nan led the ten-thousand-household force and repeatedly routed Song relief columns.

sentences.zh: 憲、潞等州複叛，骨赧引兵複取之，並收撫保德、火山而還。

translations.literal: Xian, Lu, and other prefectures rebelled again; Gu Nan led troops to retake them, and also received and pacified Baode and Huoshan before returning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian, Lu, and other prefectures rebelled again, he retook them, pacified Baode and Huoshan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 後領軍鎮夏邊，在職十二年。

translations.literal: Later he led troops to garrison the Xia frontier and held the post for twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded the Xia frontier garrison for twelve years.

sentences.zh: 天會八年，授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year 8 he was granted a hereditary meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 8 he received a hereditary meng'an.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，為天德軍節度使，致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he became military governor of Tiande Army and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianjuan he became military governor of Tiande Army and retired.

sentences.zh: 累遷開府儀同三司，卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: By successive promotions he reached Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol and died at age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Protocol and died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 子喜哥襲猛安，加宣武將軍。

translations.literal: His son Xige inherited the meng'an and was made General of Manifest Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xige inherited the meng'an and was made General of Manifest Martiality.

sentences.zh: 子 訛古乃

translations.literal: Son: E Gunai
translations.idiomatic: Son: E Gunai

sentences.zh: 訛古乃，冶訶子，姿質魁偉。

translations.literal: E Gunai was Yehe's son, imposing in stature and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: E Gunai, Yehe's son, was a man of imposing stature.

sentences.zh: 年十四，隸秦王宗翰軍中，常領兵行前為偵候。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was attached to Prince of Qin Zonghan's army and often led troops ahead as scout.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered Prince of Qin Zonghan's army and often led the van as scout.

sentences.zh: 及大軍襲遼主，訛古乃以甲騎六十，追遼招討徒山，獲之，又以七騎追獲遼公主牙不裏以獻。

translations.literal: When the great army struck at the Liao emperor, E Gunai with sixty armored horsemen pursued Liao Pacification Commissioner Tushan and captured him; with seven horsemen he also pursued and captured the Liao princess Yabulai and presented her.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army struck at the Liao emperor, E Gunai took sixty armored riders, ran down the Liao Pacification Commissioner Tushan, and captured him. With seven riders he overtook the Liao princess Yabulai and presented her as prize.

sentences.zh: 有軍來為遼援，方臨陣，中有躍馬而出者，軍帥謂之曰：「爾能為我取此乎？

translations.literal: An army came as Liao relief; as the battle lines were forming, one man leaped his horse forth from the ranks; the army commander said to him: "Can you take this man for me?
translations.idiomatic: A Liao relief army drew up for battle. One man spurred out from the line. The commander said to E Gunai: "Can you take him for me?

sentences.zh: 」訛古乃曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " E Gunai said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "I can.

sentences.zh: 」果生擒而還，問其名，曰同瓜，蓋北部中之勇者也。

translations.literal: " He indeed captured him alive and returned; asked his name, he said Tonggua—among the northern tribes a man of valor.
translations.idiomatic: " He did, and brought him back alive. The man's name was Tonggua, reckoned among the bravest of the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 訛古乃善馳驛，日能千里。

translations.literal: E Gunai was skilled at relay riding and could cover a thousand li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: E Gunai was famed for relay riding and could cover a thousand li in a day.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，屢遣將命以行。

translations.literal: When Song was attacked, he was repeatedly sent on urgent missions.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaigns against Song he was repeatedly sent on urgent dispatches.

sentences.zh: 天會八年，從秦王在燕，聞余睹反于西北，秦王令訛古乃馳驛以往，訛古乃黎明走天德，及至，日未曛也。

translations.literal: In Tianhui year 8, following the Prince of Qin at Yan, he heard Yudu had rebelled in the northwest; the prince ordered E Gunai to ride relay post thither; E Gunai set out at dawn for Tiande, and when he arrived the sun had not yet set.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 8, while with the Prince of Qin at Yan, he learned Yudu had rebelled in the northwest. The prince sent him by relay post. He left at dawn for Tiande and arrived before sunset.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年，以功授甯遠大將軍，迭刺唐古部節度使。

translations.literal: In Huangtong year 1, for his merit he was made General of Tranquil Reach and military governor of the Dieci Tanggu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 1 his service won him the rank of General of Tranquil Reach and the governorship of the Dieci Tanggu tribe.

sentences.zh: 五年，授千戶。

translations.literal: In year 5 he was granted command of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he received command of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷西北路招討使。

translations.literal: In year 6 he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 九年，再遷天德尹、西南路招討使。

translations.literal: In year 9 he was again transferred to prefect of Tiande and Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he was made prefect of Tiande and Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，召見。

translations.literal: In Tiande year 2 he was summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 he was summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷臨洮尹，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was transferred to prefect of Lintao and made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold-Purple Tally.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he became prefect of Lintao and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold-Purple Tally.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年五十三。

translations.literal: He died in office at age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 子 蒲查

translations.literal: Son: Pu Cha
translations.idiomatic: Son: Pu Cha

sentences.zh: 蒲查，自上京梅堅河徙屯天德。

translations.literal: Pu Cha moved from the Meijian River in the Upper Capital to garrison at Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Cha moved from the Meijian River in the Upper Capital to settle at Tiande.

sentences.zh: 初為元帥府紮也，使于四方稱職，按事能得其實，領猛安。

translations.literal: At first he was a zha ye of the Marshal's Office; sent to the four quarters he performed his duties well; in investigating affairs he could get at the truth; he headed a meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a staff officer of the Marshal's Office. Dispatched to the four quarters he acquitted himself well, and in investigation he always reached the truth. He headed a meng'an.

sentences.zh: 皇統間，除同知開遠軍節度使，斥候嚴整，邊境無事。

translations.literal: During Huangtong he was made Associate Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army; his scouts were strict and orderly, and the frontier was untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangtong he became Associate Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army. His scouts were strict and the frontier knew no trouble.

sentences.zh: 正隆初，為中都路兵馬判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong he became Military Affairs Judge of the Zhongdu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenglong he became Military Affairs Judge of the Zhongdu circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時，京畿多盜，蒲查捕得大盜四十余人，百姓稍安。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were numerous in the capital region; Pu Cha captured more than forty major bandits, and the common people were somewhat at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rife about the capital. Pu Cha took more than forty ringleaders, and the people breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 改安化軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Associate Military Governor of Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Associate Military Governor of Anhua Army.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，領行軍萬戶，充邳州刺史、知軍事，領本州萬戶，管所屯九猛安軍，昌武軍節度使，山東副都統。

translations.literal: In Dading year 2 he led the campaign ten-thousand-household army, served as prefect of Pizhou and director of military affairs, headed the ten-thousand households of that prefecture, administered the nine meng'an armies garrisoned there, was military governor of Changwu Army, and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 he led the campaign ten-thousand-household force as prefect of Pizhou and director of military affairs, commanded the local ten-thousand households and nine garrisoned meng'an armies, served as military governor of Changwu Army, and as Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 撒改南征，元帥府以蒲查行副統事。

translations.literal: When Sagai campaigned south, the Marshal's Office made Pu Cha acting deputy commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Sagai marched south the Marshal's Office appointed Pu Cha acting deputy commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 入為太子少詹事，再遷開遠軍節度使，襲伯父骨赧猛安，曆婆速路兵馬都總管，西北路招討使，卒。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Junior Household Master of the Heir Apparent, was again transferred to Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army, inherited his uncle Gu Nan's meng'an, served successively as overall commander of Basu circuit forces, Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Junior Household Master of the Heir Apparent, became Military Governor of Kaiyuan Army, inherited his uncle Gu Nan's meng'an, served as overall commander of Basu and as Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and died.

sentences.zh: 蒲查性廉潔忠直，臨事能斷，凡被任使，無不稱雲。

translations.literal: Pu Cha was by nature incorrupt, loyal, and upright; facing affairs he could decide; whenever entrusted with a mission, none failed to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Cha was incorrupt, loyal, and upright, decisive in action, and praised in every post entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：賢石魯與昭祖為友，歡都事景祖、世祖為之臣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Virtuous Shilu was Zhaozu's friend; Huandu served Jingzu and Shizu as their minister.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Virtuous Shilu was friend to Zhaozu; Huandu served Jingzu and Shizu as minister.

sentences.zh: 蓋金自景祖始大，諸部君臣之分始定，故傳異姓之臣，以歡都為首。

translations.literal: Jin from Jingzu's time began to grow great, and the distinction between lord and minister among the tribes was first fixed; therefore in biographies of ministers of other surnames, Huandu stands first.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingzu's day Jin began its rise, and the lord-and-minister order among the tribes was first fixed. Hence among ministers of other surnames Huandu leads the roll.

sentences.zh: 冶訶雖宗室，與歡都同功，故列敘焉。

translations.literal: Yehe, though of the imperial clan, shared merit with Huandu; therefore he is narrated here as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yehe, though of the imperial house, shared Huandu's merit, and is therefore set down here beside him.
